key_insight: A longitudinal machine learning model using routine EHR data identified incident inflammatory bowel disease months to years before diagnosis with strong external validation.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help flag patients at high risk for earlier evaluation, potentially shortening diagnostic delay in IBD care pathways.
method: Retrospective cohort of adults with IBD-compatible symptoms/findings from UCSF EHR data (2012-2024).
Incident IBD cases were confirmed with structured filtering and validated large language model note review.
Mamba and comparator models were trained on pre-diagnostic EHR data and externally tested at ZSFG without recalibration.
evidence_signal: At 6 months after presentation, Mamba achieved AUROC 0.969 at UCSF and 0.965 at ZSFG, with median lead times of 20 and 15 months, respectively.
watch_item: Because this is retrospective EHR modeling, prospective studies are still needed to confirm real-world impact, alert burden, and whether earlier identification improves outcomes.
paper_title: Prediction of incident inflammatory bowel disease from routine electronic health records: development and external validation of a longitudinal machine learning model
